Fun fact, Asians don't have any kind of genetic predisposition for being skinny/average/athletic/healthy. As a population they ARE significantly healthier than other ethnic groupings. They have better numbers in several health factors (cholesterol, blood sugar, etc.). They have better diets. They are more likely to follow healthy activity habits. HOWEVER, all evidence suggest it's entirely cultural based. When a member of asican ethnicity moves to an area outside their culture (like a family moves to america) within a rather short period (as little as a few years) they begin to exhibit the exact same statistical likelihood for obesity, diabetes, high blood pressure, etc. as the local population. Basically, they assimilate to the local cultural diet and activity habits. So Korea and other countries that are beginning to see epidemic levels of obesity, are directly correlated to a rise in "obesity culture" over native culture.
